h.en: 1.1 Occurrence of petroleum — from organic matter to a trapped deposit
h.gu: 1.1 Petroleum ની પ્રાપ્તિ — organic matter થી trapped deposit સુધી

body.en:
Definition / principle

Petroleum is a naturally occurring mixture of hydrocarbons, found as liquid crude oil and as natural gas, accumulated in porous underground rock. It was formed from buried organic matter, not from rocks themselves.

Detailed theory and conditions

Marine plants and animals died, settled on the sea floor and were buried quickly under mud before they could fully decay. That organic-rich mud became the source rock; its organic matter is called kerogen. With deeper burial, heat and time cracked kerogen first to oil and then, at higher temperature, to gas. Most oil forms in the approximate oil window of 60–150 °C; below it the kerogen is immature, above it oil is progressively converted to gas.

Oil and gas are lighter than the water in the rock pores, so they migrated upward (migration) until they were stopped. A commercial deposit therefore needs five things together: a source rock, heat and time for generation, a porous and permeable reservoir rock such as sandstone or limestone, an impermeable cap rock such as shale or salt, and a trap — an anticline (arch), a fault block or a stratigraphic pinch-out — that stops further migration. Gas, being lightest, sits at the top, oil below it and water at the bottom of the same reservoir.

Key points and data

  • Source rock: organic-rich shale; kerogen is the starting material.
  • Reservoir rock: porous (stores fluid) and permeable (allows flow) — sandstone, limestone.
  • Cap rock and trap: shale/salt seal in an anticline, fault or stratigraphic trap.
  • Indian examples: Mumbai High (offshore), Cambay basin in Gujarat, and Assam and Krishna–Godavari fields are producing petroleum regions of India.
  • Unconventional sources: shale oil/gas and oil sands hold petroleum in very low-permeability or very heavy form and need special recovery methods.

Qualification

Finding a source rock does not prove a commercial field. Occurrence is confirmed only by exploration — geological survey, seismic study and test drilling — and a deposit is useful only if the quantity, flow rate and quality justify production cost.
body.gu:
વ્યાખ્યા / સિદ્ધાંત

Petroleum એ hydrocarbons નું કુદરતી mixture છે, જે liquid crude oil તથા natural gas રૂપે છિદ્રાળુ (porous) underground rock માં મળે છે. તે rocks માંથી નહીં, દટાયેલા organic matter માંથી બન્યું છે.

વિગતવાર Theory તથા Conditions

દરિયાઈ plants તથા animals મરીને sea floor પર জমા થયા અને સંપૂર્ણ સડે તે પહેલાં mud નીચે દટાયા. તે organic-rich mud source rock બન્યું; તેમાંનું organic matter એટલે kerogen. વધુ ઊંડાણ, heat તથા time થી kerogen પહેલાં oil માં અને વધુ temperature પર gas માં crack થયું. મોટાભાગનું oil આશરે 60–150 °C ના oil window માં બને છે; તેનાથી નીચે kerogen immature રહે છે, ઉપર oil ધીમે ધીમે gas માં ફેરવાય છે.

Oil તથા gas rock pores ના water કરતાં હલકા હોવાથી ઉપર તરફ migration કરે છે, જ્યાં સુધી તેમને રોકવામાં ન આવે. તેથી commercial deposit માટે પાંચ બાબતો સાથે જોઈએ: source rock, generation માટે heat તથા time, છિદ્રાળુ અને permeable reservoir rock (sandstone કે limestone), impermeable cap rock (shale કે salt), અને migration અટકાવતો trap — anticline (arch), fault block કે stratigraphic pinch-out. એક જ reservoir માં સૌથી ઉપર gas, નીચે oil અને તળિયે water રહે છે.

મુખ્ય મુદ્દા તથા data

  • Source rock: organic-rich shale; kerogen એ starting material છે.
  • Reservoir rock: porous (fluid store કરે) તથા permeable (flow આપે) — sandstone, limestone.
  • Cap rock તથા trap: anticline, fault કે stratigraphic trap માં shale/salt seal.
  • ભારતીય examples: Mumbai High (offshore), Gujarat નું Cambay basin, Assam તથા Krishna–Godavari fields.
  • Unconventional sources: shale oil/gas તથા oil sands ને special recovery methods જોઈએ છે.

મર્યાદા / Qualification

Source rock મળવું એ commercial field નો પુરાવો નથી. Occurrence exploration — geological survey, seismic study તથા test drilling — થી જ confirm થાય છે, અને quantity, flow rate તથા quality ઉત્પાદન ખર્ચને યોગ્ય હોય તો જ deposit ઉપયોગી છે.

h.en: 1.2 Composition — elemental make-up and the four hydrocarbon families
h.gu: 1.2 Composition — elemental make-up તથા ચાર hydrocarbon families

body.en:
Definition / principle

Crude oil is not one compound. It is a mixture of thousands of hydrocarbons from light gases (C1–C4) to very large molecules (C40 and above), together with small amounts of sulfur, nitrogen, oxygen and metal compounds.

Detailed theory and conditions

The elemental composition of a typical crude is approximately: carbon 83–87 %, hydrogen 10–14 %, sulfur 0.05–6 %, nitrogen 0.1–2 %, oxygen 0.05–2 %, with traces of nickel and vanadium. Carbon and hydrogen dominate, so crude is classified by how those atoms are arranged. In paraffins (alkanes), CnH2n+2, carbon atoms form straight chains (normal paraffins) or branched chains (iso-paraffins); they give good petrol and diesel quality but the long normal paraffins separate out as wax. In naphthenes (cycloparaffins), CnH2n, carbons form saturated rings; they are good lubricant and solvent components. In aromatics, carbons form benzene rings; they raise octane number but are heavier, more toxic and soot-forming. The largest, polar molecules are grouped as resins and asphaltenes; they concentrate in the heaviest residue, raise viscosity and are the main coke-forming part of the crude.

Key points and data

  • Paraffins: chain molecules; light paraffins are gases/petrol, C17+ normal paraffins form wax.
  • Naphthenes: ring molecules; common in the middle and lubricant fractions.
  • Aromatics: benzene-ring molecules; high octane, but regulated in fuels for health reasons.
  • Asphaltenes/resins: heaviest part; stay in vacuum residue, bitumen and coke.

Qualification

These are families, not sharp divisions: one crude molecule can contain a ring, a chain and an aromatic part together. The family proportions are an average character of the crude, found from a laboratory assay, not from the crude's name or colour.
body.gu:
વ્યાખ્યા / સિદ્ધાંત

Crude oil એક compound નથી. તે હલકા gases (C1–C4) થી ખૂબ મોટા molecules (C40 થી ઉપર) સુધીના હજારો hydrocarbons નું mixture છે, સાથે sulfur, nitrogen, oxygen તથા metal compounds થોડા પ્રમાણમાં હોય છે.

વિગતવાર Theory તથા Conditions

Typical crude નું elemental composition આશરે: carbon 83–87 %, hydrogen 10–14 %, sulfur 0.05–6 %, nitrogen 0.1–2 %, oxygen 0.05–2 %, અને nickel તથા vanadium traces માં. Carbon તથા hydrogen મુખ્ય હોવાથી crude નું classification આ atoms કેવી રીતે ગોઠવાયા છે તે પરથી થાય છે. Paraffins (alkanes), CnH2n+2 માં carbon atoms straight chain (normal) કે branched chain (iso) બનાવે છે; તેઓ સારી petrol/diesel quality આપે છે, પણ લાંબા normal paraffins wax રૂપે છૂટા પડે છે. Naphthenes (cycloparaffins), CnH2n માં carbons saturated rings બનાવે છે; તેઓ સારા lubricant તથા solvent components છે. Aromatics માં benzene rings હોય છે; તેઓ octane number વધારે છે પણ ભારે, વધુ toxic તથા soot-forming છે. સૌથી મોટા, polar molecules resins તથા asphaltenes છે; તેઓ heaviest residue માં એકત્ર થાય છે, viscosity વધારે છે અને crude નો મુખ્ય coke-forming ભાગ છે.

મુખ્ય મુદ્દા તથા data

  • Paraffins: chain molecules; હલકા paraffins gases/petrol છે, C17+ normal paraffins wax બનાવે છે.
  • Naphthenes: ring molecules; middle તથા lubricant fractions માં સામાન્ય.
  • Aromatics: benzene-ring molecules; high octane, પણ health કારણોસર fuels માં regulated.
  • Asphaltenes/resins: સૌથી ભારે ભાગ; vacuum residue, bitumen તથા coke માં રહે છે.

મર્યાદા / Qualification

આ families છે, sharp divisions નથી: એક crude molecule માં ring, chain તથા aromatic ભાગ સાથે હોઈ શકે છે. Family proportions crude નું average character છે, જે laboratory assay થી મળે છે — નામ કે colour થી નહીં.

h.en: 1.2 Non-hydrocarbon part of crude — sulfur, wax, salt and why they matter
h.gu: 1.2 Crude નો non-hydrocarbon ભાગ — sulfur, wax, salt તથા તેમનું મહત્વ

body.en:
Definition / principle

A small non-hydrocarbon part decides much of the crude's behaviour: sulfur compounds (hydrogen sulfide, mercaptans and others), nitrogen and oxygen compounds, wax, asphaltenes, and the water and salt produced with the crude.

Detailed theory and conditions

Sulfur compounds corrode equipment, poison catalysts and, on burning, form sulfur oxides; that is why sulfur removal is a whole unit of this subject (Unit IV). Nitrogen compounds also poison catalysts and darken products. Oxygen compounds such as naphthenic acids corrode and form soaps with caustic. Long normal paraffins crystallise as wax when the oil cools, raising its pour point, so waxy fractions must be dewaxed (Unit IV). Asphaltenes can precipitate and foul preheat exchangers when crudes are mixed badly. Finally, crude arrives with salty formation water as an emulsion; the chlorides in that salt hydrolyse to hydrochloric acid in the hot crude unit and cause severe overhead corrosion, and the salt fouls exchangers — so the water and salt are removed first, in the desalter (Unit II).

Key points and data

  • Sulfur: corrosion, catalyst poison, SOx on burning → hydrotreating/sweetening needed.
  • Wax: crystallises on cooling → high pour point → dewaxing needed.
  • Salt and water: fouling and HCl corrosion → dehydration and desalting needed.
  • Asphaltenes: fouling and coke formation → careful blending and residue conversion.

Qualification

Two crudes of the same density can behave very differently because of this small part — one sweet and waxy, the other sour and asphaltic. Refinery design therefore starts from a full crude assay (true-boiling-point distillation and property tests), never from density alone.
body.gu:
વ્યાખ્યા / સિદ્ધાંત

નાનો non-hydrocarbon ભાગ crude ના વર્તનનો મોટો નિર્ણય કરે છે: sulfur compounds (hydrogen sulfide, mercaptans વગેરે), nitrogen તથા oxygen compounds, wax, asphaltenes, અને crude સાથે આવતું water તથા salt.

વિગતવાર Theory તથા Conditions

Sulfur compounds equipment ને corrode કરે છે, catalysts ને poison કરે છે અને બળતાં sulfur oxides બનાવે છે; તેથી sulfur removal આ subject નું આખું Unit IV છે. Nitrogen compounds પણ catalysts ને poison કરે છે અને products ઘાટા કરે છે. Naphthenic acids જેવા oxygen compounds corrode કરે છે અને caustic સાથે soaps બનાવે છે. લાંબા normal paraffins ઠંડા પડતાં wax રૂપે crystallise થાય છે અને pour point વધારે છે, તેથી waxy fractions નું dewaxing જરૂરી છે (Unit IV). Asphaltenes અયોગ્ય blending થી precipitate થઈ preheat exchangers foul કરી શકે છે. છેલ્લે, crude સાથે salty formation water emulsion રૂપે આવે છે; તે salt ના chlorides ગરમ crude unit માં hydrochloric acid બનાવી ગંભીર overhead corrosion કરે છે અને salt exchangers foul કરે છે — તેથી water તથા salt સૌથી પહેલાં desalter માં દૂર થાય છે (Unit II).

મુખ્ય મુદ્દા તથા data

  • Sulfur: corrosion, catalyst poison, બળતાં SOx → hydrotreating/sweetening જરૂરી.
  • Wax: ઠંડામાં crystallise થાય → high pour point → dewaxing જરૂરી.
  • Salt તથા water: fouling તથા HCl corrosion → dehydration તથા desalting જરૂરી.
  • Asphaltenes: fouling તથા coke formation → કાળજીપૂર્વક blending તથા residue conversion.

મર્યાદા / Qualification

સરખી density ના બે crudes આ નાના ભાગને કારણે ખૂબ જુદું વર્તન કરી શકે છે — એક sweet અને waxy, બીજો sour અને asphaltic. તેથી refinery design હંમેશા full crude assay (true-boiling-point distillation તથા property tests) થી શરૂ થાય છે, ફક્ત density થી કદી નહીં.

h.en: 1.3 Classification of crude oil — by base, by density (API) and by sulfur
h.gu: 1.3 Crude oil નું classification — base, density (API) તથા sulfur મુજબ

body.en:
Definition / principle

Crudes are classified so that a refiner can predict, before detailed design, what products a crude will give and how difficult it will be to process. The three common bases are the chemical base, the density expressed as API gravity, and the sulfur content.

Detailed theory and conditions

By chemical base, a crude whose fractions and residue are rich in paraffins (and whose residue gives wax) is paraffinic-base; one rich in naphthenes with an asphaltic residue is naphthenic (asphaltic)-base; one rich in aromatics is aromatic-base; and most crudes lie between, as mixed or intermediate-base. The Watson (UOP) characterisation factor Kw, calculated from the average boiling point and specific gravity in Numerical 1.N2, expresses the same idea numerically: higher Kw means more paraffinic.

By density, the industry uses API gravity, defined in the Formulae tab: the higher the API, the lighter the crude. The commonly used bands are light above 31.1 °API, medium 22.3–31.1, heavy 10–22.3 and extra-heavy below 10. By sulfur, a crude below about 0.5 % sulfur is called sweet and above it sour; sweet, light crudes are the easiest and most valuable because they give more light products with less treating.

Key points and data

  • Paraffinic-base: waxy, good lube and diesel character, needs dewaxing.
  • Naphthenic-base: low wax, asphaltic residue, good bitumen source.
  • Light and sweet = more valuable; heavy and sour = cheaper crude, but needs a complex (conversion) refinery.
  • Worked classification from measured data is done in Numericals 1.N1 and 1.N2.

Qualification

The API band limits and the 0.5 % sweet/sour line are industry conventions, not natural boundaries, and different books quote slightly different limits. Classification guides the first choice of refinery type; the final design always uses the crude assay.
body.gu:
વ્યાખ્યા / સિદ્ધાંત

Crudes નું classification એટલા માટે થાય છે કે detailed design પહેલાં refiner અનુમાન કરી શકે કે crude કયા products આપશે અને તેને process કરવું કેટલું અઘરું છે. ત્રણ સામાન્ય bases છે: chemical base, API gravity તરીકે density, અને sulfur content.

વિગતવાર Theory તથા Conditions

Chemical base મુજબ, જે crude ના fractions તથા residue paraffins થી ભરપૂર હોય (residue wax આપે) તે paraffinic-base; naphthenes થી ભરપૂર અને asphaltic residue વાળું naphthenic (asphaltic)-base; aromatics થી ભરપૂર aromatic-base; અને મોટાભાગના crudes વચ્ચેના, એટલે mixed કે intermediate-base છે. Watson (UOP) characterisation factor Kw, જે Numerical 1.N2 માં average boiling point તથા specific gravity થી ગણાય છે, આ જ વિચારને numerical રીતે દર્શાવે છે: વધુ Kw એટલે વધુ paraffinic.

Density મુજબ industry API gravity વાપરે છે (Formulae tab માં વ્યાખ્યા): API વધુ એટલે crude હલકું. સામાન્ય bands: light 31.1 °API થી ઉપર, medium 22.3–31.1, heavy 10–22.3, extra-heavy 10 થી નીચે. Sulfur મુજબ આશરે 0.5 % થી નીચે sulfur વાળું crude sweet અને ઉપર વાળું sour કહેવાય છે; sweet, light crudes સૌથી સરળ અને મૂલ્યવાન છે કારણ કે ઓછા treating થી વધુ light products મળે છે.

મુખ્ય મુદ્દા તથા data

  • Paraffinic-base: waxy, સારું lube તથા diesel character, dewaxing જરૂરી.
  • Naphthenic-base: low wax, asphaltic residue, bitumen નો સારો source.
  • Light તથા sweet = વધુ મૂલ્યવાન; heavy તથા sour = સસ્તું crude, પણ complex (conversion) refinery જોઈએ.
  • Measured data પરથી worked classification Numericals 1.N1 તથા 1.N2 માં છે.

મર્યાદા / Qualification

API bands તથા 0.5 % sweet/sour line industry conventions છે, કુદરતી boundaries નથી, અને જુદાં books થોડા જુદા limits આપે છે. Classification refinery type ની પ્રથમ પસંદગી માટે માર્ગદર્શન આપે છે; final design હંમેશા crude assay વાપરે છે.

h.en: 1.4 Types of refineries — from a simple topping unit to a deep-conversion refinery
h.gu: 1.4 Refineries ના પ્રકાર — સાદા topping unit થી deep-conversion refinery સુધી

body.en:
Definition / principle

A refinery is the plant that converts crude oil into useful products. Refineries are typed by how much conversion they do beyond simple distillation — that is, by their complexity.

Classification / representative type

TypeMain unitsProduct character
Topping refineryDesalter, atmospheric (and vacuum) distillation onlyOnly the fractions naturally present; large fuel-oil output
Hydro-skimming refineryTopping + naphtha hydrotreater + catalytic reformerBetter petrol quality; still no conversion of heavy residue
Conversion (cracking) refineryAbove + FCC and/or hydrocrackerHeavy fractions converted to petrol, LPG and diesel; little fuel oil
Deep-conversion (coking) refineryConversion + delayed coker / residue conversionAlmost no fuel oil; can run cheap heavy, sour crudes
Lubricant refineryVacuum distillation + solvent extraction + dewaxingLube base oils, wax and bitumen as main special products

Detailed theory and conditions

The block diagram linked to this card shows the common skeleton every type shares: crude is desalted, preheated in a pipe-still heater, separated in the atmospheric column, and the residue is separated again under vacuum; what each refinery type adds after that decides its products. A topping refinery can only sell what the crude already contains, so it suits a light crude and a fuel-oil market. As crude supply gets heavier and fuel-oil demand falls, refineries add conversion units (Unit III) that crack large molecules into petrol- and diesel-range molecules, and treating units (Unit IV) that clean the products. Petrochemical-integrated refineries go one step further and maximise naphtha, propylene and aromatics as chemical feedstocks (Unit V).

Qualification

Complexity costs money, energy and hydrogen, and it only pays when the price difference between light products and fuel oil (and between sweet and sour crude) is large enough. There is no single best type; the correct type follows the crude available and the local product market.
body.gu:
વ્યાખ્યા / સિદ્ધાંત

Refinery એ crude oil ને ઉપયોગી products માં ફેરવતો plant છે. Refineries ના પ્રકાર simple distillation થી આગળ તેઓ કેટલું conversion કરે છે તે પરથી — એટલે કે તેમની complexity પરથી — નક્કી થાય છે.

Classification / representative type

પ્રકારમુખ્ય unitsProduct character
Topping refineryફક્ત Desalter, atmospheric (તથા vacuum) distillationફક્ત કુદરતી રીતે હાજર fractions; fuel-oil output વધુ
Hydro-skimming refineryTopping + naphtha hydrotreater + catalytic reformerસારી petrol quality; heavy residue નું conversion નહીં
Conversion (cracking) refineryઉપરના + FCC અને/અથવા hydrocrackerHeavy fractions petrol, LPG તથા diesel માં ફેરવાય; fuel oil ઓછું
Deep-conversion (coking) refineryConversion + delayed coker / residue conversionલગભગ fuel oil નહીં; સસ્તા heavy, sour crudes ચલાવી શકે
Lubricant refineryVacuum distillation + solvent extraction + dewaxingLube base oils, wax તથા bitumen મુખ્ય special products

વિગતવાર Theory તથા Conditions

આ card સાથે જોડાયેલ block diagram દરેક પ્રકારમાં સામાન્ય skeleton બતાવે છે: crude desalt થાય છે, pipe-still heater માં preheat થાય છે, atmospheric column માં છૂટું પડે છે, અને residue ફરી vacuum હેઠળ છૂટું પડે છે; તે પછી દરેક refinery type જે units ઉમેરે છે તે તેના products નક્કી કરે છે. Topping refinery crude માં પહેલેથી હોય તે જ વેચી શકે છે, તેથી તે light crude તથા fuel-oil market માટે યોગ્ય છે. Crude supply ભારે થતી જાય અને fuel-oil demand ઘટે તેમ refineries conversion units (Unit III) ઉમેરે છે જે મોટા molecules ને petrol/diesel-range molecules માં crack કરે છે, અને treating units (Unit IV) products ને clean કરે છે. Petrochemical-integrated refineries એક પગલું આગળ જઈ naphtha, propylene તથા aromatics ને chemical feedstocks તરીકે મહત્તમ કરે છે (Unit V).

મર્યાદા / Qualification

Complexity માટે પૈસા, energy તથા hydrogen ખર્ચાય છે, અને તે ત્યારે જ વાજબી છે જ્યારે light products તથા fuel oil વચ્ચે (અને sweet તથા sour crude વચ્ચે) ભાવ-તફાવત પૂરતો મોટો હોય. એક જ best type નથી; યોગ્ય type ઉપલબ્ધ crude તથા સ્થાનિક product market પરથી નક્કી થાય છે.

title.en: 1.5 Refinery processes — physical and chemical changes
title.gu: 1.5 Refinery processes — physical તથા chemical changes

h.en: 1.5.1 Refinery processes involving physical changes — separation without new molecules
h.gu: 1.5.1 Physical changes વાળા refinery processes — નવા molecules વગર separation

body.en:
Definition / principle

In a physical (separation) process the molecules themselves do not change; a mixture is separated because its components differ in a physical property — boiling point, solubility, melting point or molecular size.

Working — sequence and reason

  1. Dehydration and desalting: water and salt are washed out of the crude first, to prevent fouling and corrosion in every hot unit that follows.
  2. Atmospheric distillation: the heated crude is separated by boiling range into gases/LPG, naphtha, kerosene, diesel and atmospheric residue.
  3. Vacuum distillation: the residue is distilled under vacuum so that heavy lube and gas-oil fractions boil without cracking.
  4. Solvent extraction and dewaxing: a solvent dissolves either the wanted or the unwanted part (aromatics from lube oil; oil from wax), and the two liquid phases are separated.
  5. Adsorption/clay treatment: colour- and gum-forming impurities stick to a solid surface and are removed.

Key points and data

  • Driving property: volatility (distillation), solubility (extraction), crystallisation (dewaxing), surface attraction (adsorption).
  • No catalyst and no chemical reaction; the separated parts can, in principle, be re-mixed to the original feed.
  • Physical processes cannot create more petrol than the crude naturally contains — that limit is why chemical processes exist.

Qualification

Physical separation is limited by equilibrium: one distillation stage or one extraction contact gives only a partial separation, so industrial units use many stages (a fractionating column, multi-stage extraction) to reach product specifications.
body.gu:
વ્યાખ્યા / સિદ્ધાંત

Physical (separation) process માં molecules પોતે બદલાતા નથી; mixture એટલા માટે છૂટું પડે છે કારણ કે તેના components કોઈ physical property માં જુદા છે — boiling point, solubility, melting point કે molecular size.

Working — sequence and reason

  1. Dehydration તથા desalting: crude માંથી water તથા salt સૌથી પહેલાં ધોવાય છે, જેથી પછીના દરેક hot unit માં fouling તથા corrosion અટકે.
  2. Atmospheric distillation: ગરમ crude boiling range મુજબ gases/LPG, naphtha, kerosene, diesel તથા atmospheric residue માં છૂટું પડે છે.
  3. Vacuum distillation: residue vacuum હેઠળ distill થાય છે જેથી heavy lube તથા gas-oil fractions cracking વગર ઊકળે.
  4. Solvent extraction તથા dewaxing: solvent ઇચ્છિત કે અનિચ્છિત ભાગને ઓગાળે છે (lube oil માંથી aromatics; wax માંથી oil), અને બે liquid phases છૂટા પડે છે.
  5. Adsorption/clay treatment: colour- તથા gum-forming impurities solid surface પર ચોંટીને દૂર થાય છે.

મુખ્ય મુદ્દા તથા data

  • Driving property: volatility (distillation), solubility (extraction), crystallisation (dewaxing), surface attraction (adsorption).
  • Catalyst કે chemical reaction નહીં; છૂટા પડેલા ભાગો સિદ્ધાંતમાં ફરી ભેળવીને original feed બનાવી શકાય છે.
  • Physical processes crude માં કુદરતી રીતે હોય તેનાથી વધુ petrol બનાવી શકતા નથી — આ જ મર્યાદાને કારણે chemical processes અસ્તિત્વમાં છે.

મર્યાદા / Qualification

Physical separation equilibrium થી મર્યાદિત છે: એક distillation stage કે એક extraction contact માત્ર partial separation આપે છે, તેથી industrial units product specifications સુધી પહોંચવા ઘણા stages વાપરે છે (fractionating column, multi-stage extraction).

h.en: 1.5.2 Refinery processes involving chemical changes — making new molecules
h.gu: 1.5.2 Chemical changes વાળા refinery processes — નવા molecules બનાવવા

body.en:
Definition / principle

In a chemical (conversion) process chemical bonds are broken or rearranged, so new molecules — and therefore new products — are formed. These processes exist to change both the amount and the quality of products beyond what distillation can give.

Detailed theory and conditions

Cracking breaks large, low-value molecules into smaller petrol- and LPG-range molecules, thermally or with a catalyst (Unit III). Reforming rearranges naphtha molecules over a platinum catalyst into aromatics and branched molecules of much higher octane number, and produces hydrogen as a valuable by-product (Unit III). Hydrotreating reacts a fraction with hydrogen over a catalyst to remove sulfur, nitrogen and oxygen and to saturate unstable compounds (Units III–IV). Other chemical processes used in refineries include isomerisation (straight chains to branched, for octane), alkylation (combining isobutane and butylene to a high-octane petrol component) and polymerisation of light gases. Sweetening and solvent treatments that only remove or convert the most reactive sulfur compounds are covered in Unit IV.

Comparison

PointPhysical processChemical process
MoleculesUnchanged, only separatedBroken/rearranged; new molecules formed
Can it increase petrol yield?No — limited to crude contentYes — heavy fractions are converted
Typical needsHeat, vacuum, solventCatalyst, hydrogen, high temperature/pressure

Qualification

Chemical conversion is not free improvement: it consumes hydrogen, catalyst and energy, makes some gas and coke as by-products, and needs strict safety control at high temperature and pressure. A refinery uses it only where the product value gained exceeds that cost.
body.gu:
વ્યાખ્યા / સિદ્ધાંત

Chemical (conversion) process માં chemical bonds તૂટે છે કે rearrange થાય છે, તેથી નવા molecules — અને તેથી નવા products — બને છે. આ processes distillation આપી શકે તેનાથી આગળ products નો જથ્થો તથા quality બંને બદલવા માટે છે.

વિગતવાર Theory તથા Conditions

Cracking મોટા, ઓછા-મૂલ્યના molecules ને નાના petrol- તથા LPG-range molecules માં તોડે છે, thermally કે catalyst સાથે (Unit III). Reforming naphtha molecules ને platinum catalyst પર ખૂબ વધુ octane number વાળા aromatics તથા branched molecules માં rearrange કરે છે, અને મૂલ્યવાન by-product તરીકે hydrogen ઉત્પન્ન કરે છે (Unit III). Hydrotreating fraction ને catalyst પર hydrogen સાથે react કરી sulfur, nitrogen તથા oxygen દૂર કરે છે અને unstable compounds ને saturate કરે છે (Units III–IV). Refineries માં વપરાતા અન્ય chemical processes માં isomerisation (octane માટે straight chains ને branched માં), alkylation (isobutane તથા butylene જોડી high-octane petrol component) અને light gases નું polymerisation છે. ફક્ત સૌથી reactive sulfur compounds દૂર કરતા કે convert કરતા sweetening તથા solvent treatments Unit IV માં છે.

Comparison

મુદ્દોPhysical processChemical process
Moleculesયથાવત, ફક્ત separatedતૂટે/rearrange થાય; નવા molecules બને
Petrol yield વધારી શકે?ના — crude content સુધી મર્યાદિતહા — heavy fractions convert થાય છે
સામાન્ય જરૂરિયાતોHeat, vacuum, solventCatalyst, hydrogen, high temperature/pressure

મર્યાદા / Qualification

Chemical conversion મફત improvement નથી: તે hydrogen, catalyst તથા energy વાપરે છે, by-products તરીકે થોડો gas તથા coke બનાવે છે, અને high temperature તથા pressure પર કડક safety control જોઈએ છે. Refinery તેનો ઉપયોગ ત્યારે જ કરે છે જ્યાં મળતું product value તે ખર્ચ કરતાં વધે.

h.en: 1.6 Refinery products — fuel products in order of boiling range
h.gu: 1.6 Refinery products — boiling range ના ક્રમમાં fuel products

body.en:
Definition / principle

The products of a refinery are most easily remembered as the cuts of the crude barrel in order of increasing boiling range and carbon number, from refinery gas at the top to bitumen at the bottom.

Key points and data

ProductApprox. boiling rangeMain use
Refinery gas + LPG (C3–C4)Below about 40 °CFuel gas; LPG for domestic/industrial fuel
Naphtha / petrol (gasoline)About 30–180 °CPetrol blending; naphtha as petrochemical feed
Kerosene / ATFAbout 150–275 °CJet fuel (ATF), kerosene
Diesel (gas oil)About 200–360 °CDiesel engines, furnaces
Heavy gas oil / vacuum gas oilAbove about 360 °C (vacuum cut)Feed to FCC/hydrocracker; fuel oil blending
Fuel oil / vacuum residueHeaviest liquid partIndustrial/marine fuel; feed to coker

Detailed theory and conditions

The boiling ranges overlap because a product is defined by its specification, not by a single boiling point: petrol, for example, must also meet octane, vapour-pressure and sulfur limits (Unit II, topic 2.4). Distillation alone rarely gives a finished product — naphtha must be reformed for octane, kerosene and diesel must be hydrotreated for sulfur and stability, and vacuum gas oil is usually only an intermediate feed for cracking. The linked diagram shows the same slate as boiling-range bars so that the order, and the overlaps, can be read at a glance.

Qualification

The ranges in the table are approximate teaching values. Actual cut points are moved by the refinery, within product specifications, to match crude and market demand — for example, taking more material into diesel in winter.
body.gu:
વ્યાખ્યા / સિદ્ધાંત

Refinery ના products સૌથી સહેલાઈથી crude barrel ના cuts તરીકે, વધતા boiling range તથા carbon number ના ક્રમમાં યાદ રહે છે — ઉપર refinery gas થી નીચે bitumen સુધી.

મુખ્ય મુદ્દા તથા data

Productઆશરે boiling rangeમુખ્ય ઉપયોગ
Refinery gas + LPG (C3–C4)આશરે 40 °C થી નીચેFuel gas; ઘરેલુ/industrial fuel તરીકે LPG
Naphtha / petrol (gasoline)આશરે 30–180 °CPetrol blending; petrochemical feed તરીકે naphtha
Kerosene / ATFઆશરે 150–275 °CJet fuel (ATF), kerosene
Diesel (gas oil)આશરે 200–360 °CDiesel engines, furnaces
Heavy gas oil / vacuum gas oilઆશરે 360 °C થી ઉપર (vacuum cut)FCC/hydrocracker નો feed; fuel oil blending
Fuel oil / vacuum residueસૌથી ભારે liquid ભાગIndustrial/marine fuel; coker નો feed

વિગતવાર Theory તથા Conditions

Boiling ranges overlap થાય છે કારણ કે product તેના specification થી વ્યાખ્યાયિત થાય છે, એક boiling point થી નહીં: દાખલા તરીકે petrol એ octane, vapour-pressure તથા sulfur limits પણ પૂરા કરવા પડે છે (Unit II, topic 2.4). ફક્ત distillation ભાગ્યે જ finished product આપે છે — naphtha ને octane માટે reform કરવું પડે છે, kerosene તથા diesel ને sulfur તથા stability માટે hydrotreat કરવા પડે છે, અને vacuum gas oil સામાન્ય રીતે cracking માટેનો intermediate feed જ છે. જોડાયેલ diagram આ જ slate ને boiling-range bars તરીકે બતાવે છે જેથી ક્રમ, અને overlaps, એક નજરમાં વંચાય.

મર્યાદા / Qualification

Table ના ranges આશરે teaching values છે. વાસ્તવિક cut points refinery દ્વારા, product specifications ની અંદર, crude તથા market demand મુજબ ખસેડાય છે — દાખલા તરીકે શિયાળામાં diesel માં વધુ material લેવું.

h.en: 1.6 Special and non-fuel products — lubes, wax, bitumen and petrochemical feedstocks
h.gu: 1.6 Special તથા non-fuel products — lubes, wax, bitumen તથા petrochemical feedstocks

body.en:
Definition / principle

Besides fuels, the heavier and specially treated parts of the barrel give non-fuel products — lubricating oils, greases, waxes, bitumen, solvents — and the light and aromatic streams give petrochemical feedstocks.

Key points and data

  • Lubricating oils: vacuum-distilled heavy fractions, solvent-refined and dewaxed; graded by viscosity.
  • Greases: lubricating oil thickened with a metallic soap; consistency measured by penetration (Unit II).
  • Waxes: paraffin wax separated during dewaxing; used in candles, packaging and polishes.
  • Bitumen (asphalt): the vacuum residue itself, used for road construction and roofing; its grade is set by penetration/softening point.
  • Petrochemical feedstocks: naphtha and LPG for steam cracking to ethylene/propylene, and aromatics (benzene, toluene, xylene — BTX) from reformate; developed in Unit V.
  • Other products: sulfur recovered from treating units, petroleum coke from coking, and solvents for paints and dry-cleaning.

Detailed theory and conditions

These products are the reason a refinery cannot be judged on fuel yield alone. A lube refinery earns from viscosity, viscosity-index and pour-point control of a small heavy stream; a petrochemical-integrated refinery earns by diverting naphtha that could have become petrol into ethylene and aromatics. Which slate is best is an economic optimisation over crude price, product prices and unit capacity, recalculated as markets change.

Qualification

Special products have the strictest specifications of all — a lubricant or a pharmaceutical-grade wax must meet purity and property limits that a fuel does not — so their small volume does not mean small importance, in either value or quality control.
body.gu:
વ્યાખ્યા / સિદ્ધાંત

Fuels ઉપરાંત, barrel ના ભારે અને specially treated ભાગો non-fuel products આપે છે — lubricating oils, greases, waxes, bitumen, solvents — અને light તથા aromatic streams petrochemical feedstocks આપે છે.

મુખ્ય મુદ્દા તથા data

  • Lubricating oils: vacuum-distilled heavy fractions, solvent-refined તથા dewaxed; viscosity મુજબ graded.
  • Greases: metallic soap થી ઘટ્ટ કરેલું lubricating oil; consistency penetration થી મપાય છે (Unit II).
  • Waxes: dewaxing દરમિયાન છૂટું પડતું paraffin wax; candles, packaging તથા polishes માં વપરાય છે.
  • Bitumen (asphalt): vacuum residue પોતે; road construction તથા roofing માટે; તેનો grade penetration/softening point થી નક્કી થાય છે.
  • Petrochemical feedstocks: ethylene/propylene માટે steam cracking માટે naphtha તથા LPG, અને reformate માંથી aromatics (benzene, toluene, xylene — BTX); Unit V માં વિસ્તારથી.
  • અન્ય products: treating units માંથી recovered sulfur, coking માંથી petroleum coke, અને paints તથા dry-cleaning માટે solvents.

વિગતવાર Theory તથા Conditions

આ products ને કારણે refinery ને ફક્ત fuel yield પરથી જજ કરી શકાતી નથી. Lube refinery નાની heavy stream ના viscosity, viscosity-index તથા pour-point control થી કમાય છે; petrochemical-integrated refinery petrol બની શકનારા naphtha ને ethylene તથા aromatics માં વાળીને કમાય છે. કયો slate શ્રેષ્ઠ છે તે crude price, product prices તથા unit capacity પરનું economic optimisation છે, જે markets બદલાતાં ફરી ગણાય છે.

મર્યાદા / Qualification

Special products ના specifications સૌથી કડક હોય છે — lubricant કે pharmaceutical-grade wax એ purity તથા property limits પૂરા કરવા પડે છે જે fuel એ નથી કરવા પડતા — તેથી તેમનો નાનો જથ્થો એટલે નાનું મહત્વ નહીં, value માં પણ નહીં અને quality control માં પણ નહીં.

h.en: Practical.1 Prepare a detailed chart of a modern refinery
h.gu: Practical.1 Modern refinery નો detailed chart બનાવો

body.en:
Aim and apparatus

Aim: to prepare a detailed wall chart of a modern refinery showing the units of Units I–III in flow order. Materials: chart paper or drawing software, crude/product data from this unit, and the block diagram of card 1.4.

Qualified-supervised procedure

  1. Draw the crude path first: desalter → preheat train → pipe-still heater → atmospheric column → vacuum column.
  2. Add each side product at the column where it is withdrawn, in boiling-range order from card 1.6.
  3. Add the conversion and treating units (reformer, FCC/hydrocracker, hydrotreaters) with arrows showing which fraction each one receives and returns.
  4. Label every stream with product name and one main use; mark fuel gas, LPG and bitumen at the two ends of the barrel.
  5. Present the chart and explain, for any one product, its complete path from crude to finished product.

Precautions

Do not copy a chart blindly: every arrow must be explainable. Keep process order correct — treating after distillation, conversion after vacuum distillation — even if the drawing layout is rearranged for space.

Observations and result

Record in the journal: (i) the units drawn, (ii) one product path explained, (iii) two differences between a topping and a conversion refinery found from the chart. This is a chart-preparation practical; no plant operation or measured plant data is claimed.
body.gu:
Aim and apparatus

Aim: Units I–III ના units ને flow order માં બતાવતો modern refinery નો detailed wall chart બનાવવો. Materials: chart paper કે drawing software, આ unit નો crude/product data, અને card 1.4 નો block diagram.

Qualified-supervised procedure

  1. સૌથી પહેલાં crude path દોરો: desalter → preheat train → pipe-still heater → atmospheric column → vacuum column.
  2. Card 1.6 ના boiling-range ક્રમમાં, દરેક side product તે column પર ઉમેરો જ્યાંથી તે નીકળે છે.
  3. Conversion તથા treating units (reformer, FCC/hydrocracker, hydrotreaters) એ arrows સાથે ઉમેરો કે દરેક unit કયો fraction મેળવે છે અને પાછો આપે છે.
  4. દરેક stream પર product name તથા એક મુખ્ય use લખો; barrel ના બે છેડે fuel gas, LPG તથા bitumen mark કરો.
  5. Chart present કરો અને કોઈ એક product માટે crude થી finished product સુધીનો સંપૂર્ણ path સમજાવો.

Precautions

Observations and result

h.en: Practice 1. Define petroleum and explain, with a neat sketch, the conditions needed for its occurrence and accumulation.
h.gu: Practice 1. Petroleum વ્યાખ્યાયિત કરો અને સુઘડ sketch સાથે તેની પ્રાપ્તિ તથા accumulation માટે જરૂરી conditions સમજાવો.

body.en:
Definition

Petroleum is a natural mixture of hydrocarbons occurring as crude oil and natural gas in porous rock, formed from buried organic matter.

Explanation and application

  • Source rock kerogen generates oil in the 60–150 °C oil window on burial.
  • Oil migrates upward into a porous, permeable reservoir rock.
  • An impermeable cap rock in an anticline, fault or stratigraphic trap stops it, with gas above oil above water.

Sketch: source rock below, reservoir in an arch sealed by shale, gas/oil/water layers marked (as in diagram ref1_trap).
body.gu:
વ્યાખ્યા

Petroleum એ hydrocarbons નું કુદરતી mixture છે જે crude oil તથા natural gas રૂપે છિદ્રાળુ rock માં મળે છે અને દટાયેલા organic matter માંથી બન્યું છે.

સમજૂતી તથા ઉપયોગ

  • Source rock kerogen burial પર 60–150 °C oil window માં oil generate કરે છે.
  • Oil ઉપર તરફ porous, permeable reservoir rock માં migrate થાય છે.
  • Anticline, fault કે stratigraphic trap માં impermeable cap rock તેને અટકાવે છે, gas નીચે oil અને નીચે water સાથે.

Sketch: નીચે source rock, shale થી sealed arch માં reservoir, gas/oil/water layers mark કરો (diagram ref1_trap મુજબ).

h.en: Practice 2. Describe the composition of crude oil, explaining the four hydrocarbon families with their general formulas and one refining effect of each.
h.gu: Practice 2. Crude oil નું composition વર્ણવો, ચાર hydrocarbon families તેમના general formulas તથા દરેકની એક refining effect સાથે સમજાવો.

body.en:
Definition

Crude is thousands of hydrocarbons, C 83–87 %, H 10–14 %, S 0.05–6 %, N 0.1–2 %, O 0.05–2 %, plus trace metals.

Explanation and application

  • Paraffins CnH2n+2: chains; good fuels, long ones form wax.
  • Naphthenes CnH2n: saturated rings; lube/solvent character.
  • Aromatics: benzene rings; raise octane, heavier and soot-forming.
  • Resins/asphaltenes: heaviest polar part; viscosity, fouling and coke.
body.gu:
વ્યાખ્યા

Crude હજારો hydrocarbons છે: C 83–87 %, H 10–14 %, S 0.05–6 %, N 0.1–2 %, O 0.05–2 %, સાથે trace metals.

સમજૂતી તથા ઉપયોગ

  • Paraffins CnH2n+2: chains; સારા fuels, લાંબા wax બનાવે છે.
  • Naphthenes CnH2n: saturated rings; lube/solvent character.
  • Aromatics: benzene rings; octane વધારે, ભારે તથા soot-forming.
  • Resins/asphaltenes: સૌથી ભારે polar ભાગ; viscosity, fouling તથા coke.

h.en: Practice 3. A crude has specific gravity 0.850 at 15.6 °C. Calculate its API gravity and classify it. Show every calculation step.
h.gu: Practice 3. Crude ની specific gravity 15.6 °C પર 0.850 છે. તેની API gravity ગણો અને classification કરો. દરેક calculation step બતાવો.

body.en:
Given and assumptions

SG = 0.850 at 15.6 °C. Use °API = 141.5/SG − 131.5.

Step-by-step solution

°API = 141.5/0.850 − 131.5 = 166.47 − 131.5 = 34.97.

Interpretation and check

°API = 35.0 — light crude (above 31.1). Full working in the locked numerical style is in Numerical 1.N1.
body.gu:
આપેલ તથા ધારણાઓ

SG = 0.850, 15.6 °C પર. °API = 141.5/SG − 131.5 વાપરો.

Step-by-step solution

°API = 141.5/0.850 − 131.5 = 166.47 − 131.5 = 34.97.

અર્થઘટન તથા check

°API = 35.0 — light crude (31.1 થી ઉપર). સંપૂર્ણ working locked numerical style માં Numerical 1.N1 માં છે.

h.en: Practice 4. Classify crude oil by chemical base, by API gravity and by sulfur content, stating the limits you use.
h.gu: Practice 4. Crude oil નું chemical base, API gravity તથા sulfur content મુજબ classification કરો, તમે વાપરેલા limits જણાવો.

body.en:
Definition

Classification predicts products and processing difficulty before detailed design.

Explanation and application

  • By base: paraffinic, naphthenic, aromatic, mixed — supported by Watson Kw.
  • By API: light above 31.1, medium 22.3–31.1, heavy 10–22.3, extra-heavy below 10.
  • By sulfur: sweet below about 0.5 % S, sour above.

Limits are conventions; final design uses the crude assay.
body.gu:
વ્યાખ્યા

Classification detailed design પહેલાં products તથા processing difficulty નો અંદાજ આપે છે.

સમજૂતી તથા ઉપયોગ

  • Base મુજબ: paraffinic, naphthenic, aromatic, mixed — Watson Kw થી support સાથે.
  • API મુજબ: light 31.1 થી ઉપર, medium 22.3–31.1, heavy 10–22.3, extra-heavy 10 થી નીચે.
  • Sulfur મુજબ: આશરે 0.5 % S થી નીચે sweet, ઉપર sour.

Limits conventions છે; final design crude assay વાપરે છે.

h.en: Practice 5. With a block diagram, explain the types of refineries and state which type suits a heavy, sour crude when fuel-oil demand is low.
h.gu: Practice 5. Block diagram સાથે refineries ના પ્રકાર સમજાવો અને fuel-oil demand ઓછી હોય ત્યારે heavy, sour crude માટે કયો પ્રકાર યોગ્ય છે તે જણાવો.

body.en:
Definition

Refinery types are classed by conversion complexity beyond distillation.

Explanation and application

  • Topping: distillation only. Hydro-skimming: adds hydrotreater and reformer.
  • Conversion: adds FCC/hydrocracker. Deep conversion: adds coker/residue conversion.
  • Lube type: adds solvent extraction and dewaxing.

For a heavy, sour crude with low fuel-oil demand, a deep-conversion refinery is suitable (block flow as in diagram ref1_refinery_block).
body.gu:
વ્યાખ્યા

Refinery types distillation થી આગળની conversion complexity મુજબ વર્ગીકૃત થાય છે.

સમજૂતી તથા ઉપયોગ

  • Topping: ફક્ત distillation. Hydro-skimming: hydrotreater તથા reformer ઉમેરે છે.
  • Conversion: FCC/hydrocracker ઉમેરે છે. Deep conversion: coker/residue conversion ઉમેરે છે.
  • Lube type: solvent extraction તથા dewaxing ઉમેરે છે.

ઓછી fuel-oil demand સાથે heavy, sour crude માટે deep-conversion refinery યોગ્ય છે (diagram ref1_refinery_block મુજબ block flow).

h.en: Practice 6. Distinguish between physical and chemical refinery processes, giving three examples of each and stating what each type can and cannot do.
h.gu: Practice 6. Physical તથા chemical refinery processes વચ્ચે તફાવત કરો, દરેકના ત્રણ examples આપો અને દરેક પ્રકાર શું કરી શકે અને શું ન કરી શકે તે જણાવો.

body.en:
Definition

Physical processes separate unchanged molecules; chemical processes break or rearrange bonds to form new molecules.

Comparison

  • Physical: desalting, distillation, solvent extraction/dewaxing — cannot create extra petrol.
  • Chemical: cracking, reforming, hydrotreating — can convert heavy fractions and improve quality.
  • Chemical routes cost catalyst, hydrogen and energy; physical routes are limited by equilibrium.
body.gu:
વ્યાખ્યા

Physical processes યથાવત molecules ને છૂટા પાડે છે; chemical processes bonds તોડી કે rearrange કરી નવા molecules બનાવે છે.

Comparison

  • Physical: desalting, distillation, solvent extraction/dewaxing — વધારાનું petrol બનાવી શકતા નથી.
  • Chemical: cracking, reforming, hydrotreating — heavy fractions convert કરી quality સુધારી શકે છે.
  • Chemical routes માટે catalyst, hydrogen તથા energy ખર્ચાય; physical routes equilibrium થી મર્યાદિત છે.

h.en: Practice 7. List the products of a refinery in boiling-range order with approximate ranges and one main use of each, and explain why a boiling range alone does not make a finished product.
h.gu: Practice 7. Refinery ના products boiling-range ના ક્રમમાં આશરે ranges તથા દરેકના એક મુખ્ય ઉપયોગ સાથે જણાવો, અને ફક્ત boiling range finished product કેમ બનાવતું નથી તે સમજાવો.

body.en:
Definition

Products follow the barrel in boiling-range order.

Key points and data

  • LPG below ~40 °C; petrol ~30–180 °C; kerosene/ATF ~150–275 °C; diesel ~200–360 °C; VGO above ~360 °C; residue last.
  • Uses: LPG fuel, petrol engines, jet fuel, diesel engines, cracking feed, fuel/bitumen.

A range alone is not a finished product because octane, vapour pressure, sulfur and other specifications must also be met.
body.gu:
વ્યાખ્યા

Products barrel ને boiling-range ક્રમમાં અનુસરે છે.

મુખ્ય મુદ્દા તથા data

  • LPG આશરે 40 °C થી નીચે; petrol ~30–180 °C; kerosene/ATF ~150–275 °C; diesel ~200–360 °C; VGO ~360 °C થી ઉપર; residue છેલ્લે.
  • ઉપયોગો: LPG fuel, petrol engines, jet fuel, diesel engines, cracking feed, fuel/bitumen.

ફક્ત range finished product બનાવતું નથી કારણ કે octane, vapour pressure, sulfur તથા અન્ય specifications પણ પૂરા થવા જોઈએ.

h.en: Practice 8. Explain how the non-hydrocarbon part of crude — sulfur, wax, asphaltenes and salt — decides which treating and conversion units a refinery must install.
h.gu: Practice 8. Crude નો non-hydrocarbon ભાગ — sulfur, wax, asphaltenes તથા salt — refinery એ કયા treating તથા conversion units સ્થાપવા પડશે તે કેવી રીતે નક્કી કરે છે તે સમજાવો.

body.en:
Definition

The small non-hydrocarbon part controls corrosion, catalyst life and product quality.

Explanation and application

  • Sulfur → hydrotreating, sweetening, desulfurisation (Unit IV) and sulfur recovery.
  • Salt/water → desalting before heating; wax → dewaxing; asphaltenes → blending care and residue conversion/coking.

Hence a sour, waxy, asphaltic crude forces a more complex and costly refinery than a sweet light crude.
body.gu:
વ્યાખ્યા

નાનો non-hydrocarbon ભાગ corrosion, catalyst life તથા product quality નિયંત્રિત કરે છે.

સમજૂતી તથા ઉપયોગ

  • Sulfur → hydrotreating, sweetening, desulfurisation (Unit IV) તથા sulfur recovery.
  • Salt/water → ગરમ કરતા પહેલાં desalting; wax → dewaxing; asphaltenes → blending care તથા residue conversion/coking.

તેથી sour, waxy, asphaltic crude sweet light crude કરતાં વધુ complex તથા મોંઘી refinery ફરજ પાડે છે.

q.en: Numerical 1.N1: A crude sample has specific gravity 0.850 at 15.6 °C. Calculate its API gravity and classify the crude.
q.gu: Numerical 1.N1: Crude sample ની specific gravity 15.6 °C પર 0.850 છે. તેની API gravity ગણો અને crude નું classification કરો.

a.en:
Given

Specific gravity of crude, SG = 0.850 at 15.6 °C (60 °F), referred to water at the same temperature.

Find

Find the API gravity and state whether the crude is light, medium, heavy or extra-heavy.

Formula

°API = 141.5 / SG − 131.5

Substitution and calculation

°API = 141.5 / 0.850 − 131.5
°API = 166.47 − 131.5
°API = 34.97

Final answer with units

°API = 35.0 °API
Classification: Light crude (above 31.1 °API)

Validity check

The crude is lighter than water (SG below 1), so a positive API well above 10 is expected. The value 35.0 lies just above the 31.1 light-crude limit, so the classification is light — but it is close to the medium band, so the full assay, not API alone, decides the processing route.
a.gu:
આપેલ

Crude ની specific gravity, SG = 0.850, 15.6 °C (60 °F) પર, સરખા temperature ના water ના સંદર્ભમાં.

શોધો

API gravity શોધો અને crude light, medium, heavy કે extra-heavy છે તે જણાવો.

સૂત્ર

°API = 141.5 / SG − 131.5

Substitution તથા Calculation

°API = 141.5 / 0.850 − 131.5
°API = 166.47 − 131.5
°API = 34.97

Units સાથે અંતિમ જવાબ

°API = 35.0 °API
Classification: Light crude (31.1 °API થી ઉપર)

Validity Check

Crude water કરતાં હલકું છે (SG 1 થી નીચે), તેથી 10 કરતાં સારો એવો positive API અપેક્ષિત છે. 35.0 નું મૂલ્ય 31.1 ની light-crude limit થી થોડું જ ઉપર છે, તેથી classification light છે — પણ તે medium band ની નજીક છે, તેથી processing route ફક્ત API નહીં, full assay નક્કી કરે છે.

q.en: Numerical 1.N2: A crude fraction has mean average boiling point 300 °C and specific gravity 0.820. Calculate the Watson (UOP) characterisation factor Kw and state the character of the fraction.
q.gu: Numerical 1.N2: Crude fraction નો mean average boiling point 300 °C તથા specific gravity 0.820 છે. Watson (UOP) characterisation factor Kw ગણો અને fraction નું character જણાવો.

a.en:
Given

Mean average boiling point, MeABP = 300 °C; specific gravity, SG = 0.820. Watson factor needs the boiling point on an absolute (Rankine) scale.

Find

Find Kw and state whether the fraction is paraffinic, intermediate, naphthenic or aromatic in character.

Formula

Kw = (TB)1/3 / SG, with TB in Rankine (°R)
TB (°R) = [MeABP (°C) + 273.15] × 1.8

Substitution and calculation

TB = (300 + 273.15) × 1.8 = 1031.67 °R
(TB)1/3 = (1031.67)1/3 = 10.10
Kw = 10.10 / 0.820 = 12.32

Final answer with units

Kw = 12.3 (dimensionless)
Character: Paraffinic (Kw above about 12.1)

Validity check

Kw for real petroleum fractions always falls roughly between 10 and 13, and 12.3 is inside that band. A common error is to use Celsius directly: (300)1/3/0.820 = 8.2, which is outside the possible band and immediately shows the absolute-scale step was missed.
a.gu:
આપેલ

Mean average boiling point, MeABP = 300 °C; specific gravity, SG = 0.820. Watson factor માટે boiling point absolute (Rankine) scale પર જોઈએ છે.

શોધો

Kw શોધો અને fraction paraffinic, intermediate, naphthenic કે aromatic character નું છે તે જણાવો.

સૂત્ર

Kw = (TB)1/3 / SG, જ્યાં TB Rankine (°R) માં
TB (°R) = [MeABP (°C) + 273.15] × 1.8

Substitution તથા Calculation

TB = (300 + 273.15) × 1.8 = 1031.67 °R
(TB)1/3 = (1031.67)1/3 = 10.10
Kw = 10.10 / 0.820 = 12.32

Units સાથે અંતિમ જવાબ

Kw = 12.3 (dimensionless)
Character: Paraffinic (Kw આશરે 12.1 થી ઉપર)

Validity Check

વાસ્તવિક petroleum fractions માટે Kw હંમેશા આશરે 10 થી 13 વચ્ચે હોય છે, અને 12.3 તે band માં છે. સામાન્ય ભૂલ Celsius સીધો વાપરવાની છે: (300)1/3/0.820 = 8.2, જે શક્ય band ની બહાર છે અને તરત બતાવે છે કે absolute-scale step ચૂકી ગયું છે.

q.en: Numerical 1.N3: 1000 kg of crude is distilled in a topping unit. Illustrative yields are: refinery gas and loss 3 %, LPG 3 %, petrol 18 %, kerosene 12 %, diesel 28 %, vacuum gas oil 20 % and residue 16 % by mass. Calculate the mass of each stream and check the balance.
q.gu: Numerical 1.N3: Topping unit માં 1000 kg crude distill થાય છે. Illustrative yields છે: refinery gas તથા loss 3 %, LPG 3 %, petrol 18 %, kerosene 12 %, diesel 28 %, vacuum gas oil 20 % અને residue 16 % (mass મુજબ). દરેક stream નો mass ગણો અને balance check કરો.

a.en:
Given

Feed F = 1000 kg crude. Illustrative mass yields: gas + loss 3 %, LPG 3 %, petrol 18 %, kerosene 12 %, diesel 28 %, vacuum gas oil 20 %, residue 16 %. Yields sum to 100 %. These are teaching yields, not measured plant data.

Find

Find the mass of each product stream and verify the overall mass balance.

Formula

Mass of product = F × (yield % / 100)
F = sum of all product masses + gas and loss

Substitution and calculation

Gas + loss = 1000 × 0.03 = 30 kg
LPG = 1000 × 0.03 = 30 kg
Petrol = 1000 × 0.18 = 180 kg
Kerosene = 1000 × 0.12 = 120 kg
Diesel = 1000 × 0.28 = 280 kg
Vacuum gas oil = 1000 × 0.20 = 200 kg
Residue = 1000 × 0.16 = 160 kg
Total out = 30 + 30 + 180 + 120 + 280 + 200 + 160 = 1000 kg

Final answer with units

Petrol = 180 kg, Kerosene = 120 kg, Diesel = 280 kg
LPG = 30 kg, VGO = 200 kg, Residue = 160 kg, Gas + loss = 30 kg

Validity check

Total out = 1000 kg = feed, so the balance closes exactly, as it must for stated yields. In a real unit the yields are measured and a small unaccounted loss remains; if a calculated total differs from the feed, a yield or a stream has been missed — the balance, not the feed figure, is corrected first.
a.gu:
આપેલ

Feed F = 1000 kg crude. Illustrative mass yields: gas + loss 3 %, LPG 3 %, petrol 18 %, kerosene 12 %, diesel 28 %, vacuum gas oil 20 %, residue 16 %. Yields નો સરવાળો 100 % થાય છે. આ teaching yields છે, measured plant data નથી.

શોધો

દરેક product stream નો mass શોધો અને overall mass balance verify કરો.

સૂત્ર

Product નો mass = F × (yield % / 100)
F = બધા product masses નો સરવાળો + gas તથા loss

Substitution તથા Calculation

Gas + loss = 1000 × 0.03 = 30 kg
LPG = 1000 × 0.03 = 30 kg
Petrol = 1000 × 0.18 = 180 kg
Kerosene = 1000 × 0.12 = 120 kg
Diesel = 1000 × 0.28 = 280 kg
Vacuum gas oil = 1000 × 0.20 = 200 kg
Residue = 1000 × 0.16 = 160 kg
Total out = 30 + 30 + 180 + 120 + 280 + 200 + 160 = 1000 kg

Units સાથે અંતિમ જવાબ

Petrol = 180 kg, Kerosene = 120 kg, Diesel = 280 kg
LPG = 30 kg, VGO = 200 kg, Residue = 160 kg, Gas + loss = 30 kg

Validity Check

Total out = 1000 kg = feed, તેથી balance બરાબર close થાય છે, જે stated yields માટે થવું જ જોઈએ. વાસ્તવિક unit માં yields મપાય છે અને નાનો unaccounted loss રહે છે; જો ગણેલો total feed થી જુદો આવે, તો કોઈ yield કે stream ચૂકી ગયો છે — પહેલાં balance સુધારાય છે, feed figure નહીં.

terms.en: Higher °API = lighter crude. Bands: light above 31.1, medium 22.3–31.1, heavy 10–22.3, extra-heavy below 10.
terms.gu: વધુ °API = હલકું crude. Bands: light 31.1 થી ઉપર, medium 22.3–31.1, heavy 10–22.3, extra-heavy 10 થી નીચે.

items.f: SG = density of oil / density of water at the same temperature

terms.en: Water has SG 1.000 and 10 °API. Most crudes: SG about 0.80–0.95.
terms.gu: Water નો SG 1.000 અને 10 °API છે. મોટાભાગના crudes: SG આશરે 0.80–0.95.

items.f: Kw = (TB)^(1/3) / SG,  TB = mean average boiling point in °R

terms.en: Above ~12.1 paraffinic; 11.5–12.1 intermediate; 11.0–11.5 naphthenic; below 11 aromatic. TB must be absolute.
terms.gu: આશરે 12.1 થી ઉપર paraffinic; 11.5–12.1 intermediate; 11.0–11.5 naphthenic; 11 થી નીચે aromatic. TB absolute જ હોવો જોઈએ.

items.f: Sweet: sulfur below about 0.5 % by mass;  Sour: above about 0.5 %

terms.en: A convention, not a law of nature; sour crudes need desulfurisation (Unit IV) and usually sell cheaper.
terms.gu: એક convention છે, કુદરતી નિયમ નથી; sour crudes ને desulfurisation (Unit IV) જોઈએ છે અને સામાન્ય રીતે સસ્તા વેચાય છે.

items.f: Yield % of a product = (mass or volume of product / feed) × 100

terms.en: State whether the yield is on mass or volume basis; the two differ because products have different densities.
terms.gu: Yield mass કે volume basis પર છે તે જણાવો; બંને જુદા પડે છે કારણ કે products ની densities જુદી છે.

items.f: Feed = all products + fuel consumed + loss

terms.en: Every unit calculation starts here. A balance that does not close means a missed stream, not new matter.
terms.gu: દરેક unit calculation અહીંથી શરૂ થાય છે. Close ન થતો balance એટલે ચૂકાયેલો stream, નવું matter નહીં.

items.f: 1 barrel (bbl) = 42 US gallons ≈ 159 litres;  1 m³ ≈ 6.29 bbl

terms.en: Refinery capacities are quoted in barrels per day. Mass per barrel varies with crude density — there is no fixed kg-per-barrel.
terms.gu: Refinery capacities barrels per day માં દર્શાવાય છે. Barrel દીઠ mass crude density મુજબ બદલાય છે — નિશ્ચિત kg-per-barrel નથી.

title.en: Unit 1 viva — occurrence, composition, classification, refinery types and products
title.gu: Unit 1 viva — occurrence, composition, classification, refinery types તથા products

q.en: What is petroleum?
q.gu: Petroleum એટલે શું?

a.en: Petroleum is a naturally occurring mixture of hydrocarbons, found as liquid crude oil and natural gas in porous underground rock, formed from buried organic matter.
a.gu: Petroleum એ hydrocarbons નું કુદરતી mixture છે, જે liquid crude oil તથા natural gas રૂપે છિદ્રાળુ underground rock માં મળે છે અને દટાયેલા organic matter માંથી બન્યું છે.

q.en: Name the five conditions needed for a commercial oil deposit.
q.gu: Commercial oil deposit માટે જરૂરી પાંચ conditions જણાવો.

a.en: A source rock with kerogen, heat and time for generation (the oil window), migration, a porous-permeable reservoir rock, and an impermeable cap rock with a trap.
a.gu: Kerogen વાળો source rock, generation માટે heat તથા time (oil window), migration, porous-permeable reservoir rock, અને trap સાથે impermeable cap rock.

q.en: What is kerogen and the oil window?
q.gu: Kerogen તથા oil window એટલે શું?

a.en: Kerogen is the solid organic matter in source rock that cracks on burial heating, first to oil and then to gas. The oil window is the approximate 60–150 °C range in which most oil forms.
a.gu: Kerogen એ source rock માંનું solid organic matter છે જે burial heating થી પહેલાં oil અને પછી gas માં crack થાય છે. Oil window એ આશરે 60–150 °C નો range છે જેમાં મોટાભાગનું oil બને છે.

q.en: Name the four hydrocarbon families in crude oil.
q.gu: Crude oil ની ચાર hydrocarbon families જણાવો.

a.en: Paraffins (chain alkanes), naphthenes (saturated rings), aromatics (benzene rings), and resins/asphaltenes (the heaviest, polar part).
a.gu: Paraffins (chain alkanes), naphthenes (saturated rings), aromatics (benzene rings), અને resins/asphaltenes (સૌથી ભારે, polar ભાગ).

q.en: Why must crude be desalted before heating?
q.gu: Crude ને ગરમ કરતા પહેલાં desalt કેમ કરવું પડે છે?

a.en: The salt, present in produced water, fouls preheat exchangers and its chlorides form hydrochloric acid at high temperature, causing severe corrosion in the crude unit overhead system.
a.gu: Produced water માં રહેલું salt preheat exchangers foul કરે છે અને તેના chlorides ઊંચા temperature પર hydrochloric acid બનાવી crude unit overhead system માં ગંભીર corrosion કરે છે.

q.en: Define API gravity. Is a 40 °API crude lighter or heavier than a 20 °API crude?
q.gu: API gravity વ્યાખ્યાયિત કરો. 40 °API crude 20 °API crude કરતાં હલકું છે કે ભારે?

a.en: API gravity = 141.5/SG − 131.5 and measures lightness: the higher the API, the lighter the oil. A 40 °API crude is therefore much lighter than a 20 °API crude.
a.gu: API gravity = 141.5/SG − 131.5 અને હલકાપણું માપે છે: API વધુ એટલે oil હલકું. તેથી 40 °API crude 20 °API crude કરતાં ઘણું હલકું છે.

q.en: What do sweet and sour crude mean?
q.gu: Sweet તથા sour crude એટલે શું?

a.en: By a common convention, a crude with less than about 0.5 % sulfur is sweet and one with more is sour. Sour crudes need desulfurisation and are cheaper to buy but costlier to process.
a.gu: સામાન્ય convention મુજબ, આશરે 0.5 % થી ઓછું sulfur હોય તે crude sweet અને વધુ હોય તે sour છે. Sour crudes ને desulfurisation જોઈએ છે અને ખરીદવામાં સસ્તા પણ process કરવામાં મોંઘા પડે છે.

q.en: What does the Watson factor Kw tell you?
q.gu: Watson factor Kw શું દર્શાવે છે?

a.en: Kw = (mean average boiling point in °R)^(1/3)/SG expresses chemical character: above about 12.1 the fraction is paraffinic, near 11 naphthenic and below 11 aromatic.
a.gu: Kw = (mean average boiling point °R માં)^(1/3)/SG chemical character દર્શાવે છે: આશરે 12.1 થી ઉપર fraction paraffinic, 11 ની આસપાસ naphthenic અને 11 થી નીચે aromatic.

q.en: Give one physical and one chemical refinery process.
q.gu: એક physical અને એક chemical refinery process આપો.

a.en: Distillation is physical — molecules are only separated by boiling point. Cracking is chemical — large molecules are broken into smaller petrol- and LPG-range molecules.
a.gu: Distillation physical છે — molecules ફક્ત boiling point થી છૂટા પડે છે. Cracking chemical છે — મોટા molecules નાના petrol- તથા LPG-range molecules માં તૂટે છે.

q.en: How does a topping refinery differ from a conversion refinery?
q.gu: Topping refinery conversion refinery થી કેવી રીતે જુદી પડે છે?

a.en: A topping refinery only distils crude, so it can sell only the fractions naturally present and makes much fuel oil. A conversion refinery adds FCC/hydrocracking (and similar) units that convert heavy fractions into petrol, LPG and diesel.
a.gu: Topping refinery ફક્ત crude distill કરે છે, તેથી કુદરતી રીતે હાજર fractions જ વેચી શકે છે અને ઘણું fuel oil બનાવે છે. Conversion refinery FCC/hydrocracking (અને સમાન) units ઉમેરે છે જે heavy fractions ને petrol, LPG તથા diesel માં ફેરવે છે.

q.en: Name the refinery products in boiling-range order.
q.gu: Refinery products boiling-range ના ક્રમમાં જણાવો.

a.en: Refinery gas and LPG, naphtha/petrol, kerosene/ATF, diesel, vacuum gas oil, then fuel oil and vacuum residue (bitumen/coke feed) as the heaviest products.
a.gu: Refinery gas તથા LPG, naphtha/petrol, kerosene/ATF, diesel, vacuum gas oil, પછી સૌથી ભારે products તરીકે fuel oil તથા vacuum residue (bitumen/coke feed).

q.en: Why can distillation alone not maximise petrol production?
q.gu: ફક્ત distillation petrol production મહત્તમ કેમ કરી શકતું નથી?

a.en: Because distillation only separates the petrol-range molecules already present in the crude; it creates none. Extra petrol comes only from chemical conversion of heavier fractions, by cracking and reforming.
a.gu: કારણ કે distillation ફક્ત crude માં પહેલેથી હાજર petrol-range molecules ને જ છૂટા પાડે છે; તે એક પણ બનાવતું નથી. વધારાનું petrol ફક્ત ભારે fractions ના chemical conversion — cracking તથા reforming — થી જ મળે છે.

q.en: Practice: Define petroleum and explain, with a neat sketch, the conditions needed for its occurrence and accumulation.
q.gu: Practice: Petroleum વ્યાખ્યાયિત કરો અને સુઘડ sketch સાથે તેની પ્રાપ્તિ તથા accumulation માટે જરૂરી conditions સમજાવો.

q.en: Practice: Describe the composition of crude oil, explaining the four hydrocarbon families with their general formulas and one refining effect of each.
q.gu: Practice: Crude oil નું composition વર્ણવો, ચાર hydrocarbon families તેમના general formulas તથા દરેકની એક refining effect સાથે સમજાવો.

q.en: Practice: A crude has specific gravity 0.850 at 15.6 °C. Calculate its API gravity and classify it. Show every calculation step.
q.gu: Practice: Crude ની specific gravity 15.6 °C પર 0.850 છે. તેની API gravity ગણો અને classification કરો. દરેક calculation step બતાવો.

q.en: Practice: Classify crude oil by chemical base, by API gravity and by sulfur content, stating the limits you use.
q.gu: Practice: Crude oil નું chemical base, API gravity તથા sulfur content મુજબ classification કરો, તમે વાપરેલા limits જણાવો.

q.en: Practice: With a block diagram, explain the types of refineries and state which type suits a heavy, sour crude when fuel-oil demand is low.
q.gu: Practice: Block diagram સાથે refineries ના પ્રકાર સમજાવો અને fuel-oil demand ઓછી હોય ત્યારે heavy, sour crude માટે કયો પ્રકાર યોગ્ય છે તે જણાવો.

q.en: Practice: Distinguish between physical and chemical refinery processes, giving three examples of each and stating what each type can and cannot do.
q.gu: Practice: Physical તથા chemical refinery processes વચ્ચે તફાવત કરો, દરેકના ત્રણ examples આપો અને દરેક પ્રકાર શું કરી શકે અને શું ન કરી શકે તે જણાવો.

q.en: Practice: List the products of a refinery in boiling-range order with approximate ranges and one main use of each, and explain why a boiling range alone does not make a finished product.
q.gu: Practice: Refinery ના products boiling-range ના ક્રમમાં આશરે ranges તથા દરેકના એક મુખ્ય ઉપયોગ સાથે જણાવો, અને ફક્ત boiling range finished product કેમ બનાવતું નથી તે સમજાવો.

q.en: Practice: Explain how the non-hydrocarbon part of crude — sulfur, wax, asphaltenes and salt — decides which treating and conversion units a refinery must install.
q.gu: Practice: Crude નો non-hydrocarbon ભાગ — sulfur, wax, asphaltenes તથા salt — refinery એ કયા treating તથા conversion units સ્થાપવા પડશે તે કેવી રીતે નક્કી કરે છે તે સમજાવો.

title.en: Prepare a detailed chart of a modern refinery
title.gu: Modern refinery નો detailed chart બનાવો

body.en:
Aim and apparatus

Aim: to prepare a detailed wall chart of a modern refinery showing the units of Units I–III in flow order. Materials: chart paper or drawing software, crude/product data from this unit, and the block diagram of card 1.4.

Qualified-supervised procedure

  1. Draw the crude path first: desalter → preheat train → pipe-still heater → atmospheric column → vacuum column.
  2. Add each side product at the column where it is withdrawn, in boiling-range order from card 1.6.
  3. Add the conversion and treating units (reformer, FCC/hydrocracker, hydrotreaters) with arrows showing which fraction each one receives and returns.
  4. Label every stream with product name and one main use; mark fuel gas, LPG and bitumen at the two ends of the barrel.
  5. Present the chart and explain, for any one product, its complete path from crude to finished product.

Precautions

Do not copy a chart blindly: every arrow must be explainable. Keep process order correct — treating after distillation, conversion after vacuum distillation — even if the drawing layout is rearranged for space.

Observations and result

Record in the journal: (i) the units drawn, (ii) one product path explained, (iii) two differences between a topping and a conversion refinery found from the chart. This is a chart-preparation practical; no plant operation or measured plant data is claimed.
body.gu:
Aim and apparatus

Aim: Units I–III ના units ને flow order માં બતાવતો modern refinery નો detailed wall chart બનાવવો. Materials: chart paper કે drawing software, આ unit નો crude/product data, અને card 1.4 નો block diagram.

Qualified-supervised procedure

  1. સૌથી પહેલાં crude path દોરો: desalter → preheat train → pipe-still heater → atmospheric column → vacuum column.
  2. Card 1.6 ના boiling-range ક્રમમાં, દરેક side product તે column પર ઉમેરો જ્યાંથી તે નીકળે છે.
  3. Conversion તથા treating units (reformer, FCC/hydrocracker, hydrotreaters) એ arrows સાથે ઉમેરો કે દરેક unit કયો fraction મેળવે છે અને પાછો આપે છે.
  4. દરેક stream પર product name તથા એક મુખ્ય use લખો; barrel ના બે છેડે fuel gas, LPG તથા bitumen mark કરો.
  5. Chart present કરો અને કોઈ એક product માટે crude થી finished product સુધીનો સંપૂર્ણ path સમજાવો.

Precautions

Chart આંધળું copy ન કરો: દરેક arrow સમજાવી શકાય તેવો હોવો જોઈએ. Drawing layout જગ્યા માટે બદલાય તો પણ process order સાચો રાખો — treating distillation પછી, conversion vacuum distillation પછી.

Observations and result

Journal માં નોંધો: (i) દોરેલા units, (ii) સમજાવેલો એક product path, (iii) chart પરથી મળેલા topping તથા conversion refinery વચ્ચેના બે તફાવત. આ chart-preparation practical છે; કોઈ plant operation કે measured plant data નો દાવો નથી.
